walkthroughs.body_html:
A food chain shows energy flow.

Only about 10% of energy passes to the next trophic level.

So top predators are rare.

Nutrients move in a cycle.

Three stores: biomass, litter and soil.

In rainforests, biomass dominates; in tundra, litter does.

Climate decides biome.

Latitude controls sunlight; altitude controls temperature.

Ocean currents shift rainfall: e.g. the Atacama is dry because of cold currents.

mcqs.q: What weather does an anticyclone (high pressure system) bring?
options: Anticyclones bring heavy rainfall because they trap moisture.
Climate change only happens in summer.
Descending air warms and dries, suppressing cloud formation — so anticyclones bring clear, settled weather: hot in summer, cold and frosty in winter.
High pressure brings stormy weather because the air pushes down hard.

mcqs.q: What drives the movement of tectonic plates?
options: Climate change only happens in summer.
Convection currents in the mantle combined with slab pull at subduction zones and ridge push at constructive boundaries.
The Earth's rotation makes the plates move.
Plates move because of ocean tides pulling on the crust.

mcqs.q: Why can a cold winter NOT disprove climate change?
options: Climate change only happens in summer.
Anticyclones bring heavy rainfall because they trap moisture.
A really cold winter proves global warming is not happening.
Climate is the long-term statistical average; a single cold winter is a weather event. Climate change is the trend in averages and extremes over decades, not the absence of cold days.
